translations.text: Since many have undertaken to write accounts of the events that have been firmly believed among us,
just as they were handed down to us by those who saw them with their own eyes from the beginning and became servants of the word,
I too decided, after carefully following everything from the beginning, to write it all down for you in order, most excellent Theophilus,
so that you may know the certainty of the things you have been taught.
In the days of Herod, king of Judea, there was a priest named Zechariah who belonged to the priestly division of Abijah. He had a wife descended from Aaron, and her name was Elizabeth.
Both of them were righteous before God, following all the Lord's commandments and ordinances and living holy lives.
They had no child because Elizabeth was barren, and both of them were advanced in age.
While he was serving before God during his division's appointed turn,
according to the custom of the priesthood, it fell to him to offer incense, and he entered the Lord's temple.
The whole crowd of people was praying outside at the time of the incense offering.
An angel of the Lord appeared to him, standing to the right of the incense altar.
Zechariah was troubled when he saw him, and fear came over him.
The angel of the Lord said to him, “Do not be afraid, Zechariah, because your prayer has been heard. Your wife Elizabeth will bear you a son, and you will name him John.
You will have joy and gladness, and many will rejoice at his birth.
For he will be great before the Lord. He will drink neither wine nor strong drink, and he will be filled with the Holy Spirit from the time he is in his mother's womb.
He will turn many of the children of Israel back to the Lord their God.

He will go before him in the spirit and power of Elijah, to turn the hearts of fathers toward their children and the disobedient to the wisdom of the righteous, to prepare a people ready for the Lord.”
Zechariah said to the angel, “How will I know this? For I am old, and my wife is advanced in age.”
The angel answered him, “I am Gabriel, who stands before God. I was sent to speak with you and announce these things to you.
Look, you will remain silent and unable to speak until the day these things happen, because you did not believe my words, which will be fulfilled at their appointed time.”
The people were waiting for Zechariah, and they wondered why he was taking so long in the temple.
When he came out, he could not speak to them, and they realized that he had seen a vision in the temple. He was making signs to them and remained unable to speak.
When the days of his service were completed, he went home.
After those days, his wife Elizabeth became pregnant, and she kept herself hidden for five months, saying,
“This is what the Lord has done for me in the days when he looked upon me to take away my disgrace among people.”
In the sixth month, the angel Gabriel was sent by God to a town in Galilee named Nazareth.
To a virgin betrothed to a man named Joseph, from the house of David. The virgin’s name was Mary.
When he came in to her, he said to her, “Greetings, you who have found favor! The Lord is with you.”
But she was troubled by these words and wondered what kind of greeting this was.
The angel said to her, “Do not be afraid, Mary, for you have found favor with God.
Look, you will conceive and give birth to a son, and you will name him Jesus.
He will be great and will be called the Son of the Most High. The Lord God will give him the throne of his father David.
He will reign over the house of Jacob forever, and his kingdom will have no end.”
But Mary said to the angel, “How will this happen, since I have not had sexual relations with a man?”
The angel answered her, “The Holy Spirit will come down upon you, and the power of the Most High will overshadow you. Therefore the holy one who will be born will be called the Son of God.”
“And look, your relative Elizabeth has also conceived a son in her old age. This is the sixth month for her who was called barren.
For no word will be powerless before God.”
Mary said, “Look, I am the Lord’s servant. Let it happen to me according to your word.” And the angel left her.
In those days Mary got up and went quickly into the hill country, to the city in Judea.
She entered Zechariah’s house and greeted Elizabeth.
When Elizabeth heard Mary’s greeting, the baby moved inside her, and Elizabeth was filled with the Holy Spirit.
She raised her voice loudly and said, “Blessed are you among women, and blessed is the fruit of your womb!
Who am I that the mother of my Lord should come to me?
For look, when the sound of your greeting reached my ears, the baby moved with joy inside me.
And blessed is she who believed that the things spoken to her by the Lord would be fulfilled.”
And Mary said, “My soul exalts the Lord,
and my spirit has rejoiced in God my Savior,
because he has looked down upon the lowly condition of his servant. For look, from now on every generation will call me blessed,
because the Mighty One has done great things for me, and his name is holy.
His mercy is upon those who fear him, from generation to generation.
He has shown strength with his arm. He has scattered those who are proud in the thoughts of their hearts.
He has brought rulers down from their thrones and lifted up the lowly.
He filled the hungry with good things and sent the rich away empty.
He helped Israel his servant, remembering his mercy.
Just as he spoke to our ancestors, to Abraham and his descendants forever.
Mary stayed with her for three months and then returned to her home.
The time came for Elizabeth to give birth, and she gave birth to a son.
Her neighbors and relatives heard that the Lord had shown her great mercy, and they rejoiced with her.
On the eighth day they came to circumcise the child, and they called him Zechariah after his father.
But his mother answered, “No! He will be called John.”
They said to her, “No one among your relatives is called by that name.”
They made signs to his father, asking, “What do you want to call him?”
He asked for a writing tablet and wrote, “His name is John.” They were all amazed.
Immediately his mouth opened and his tongue was freed, and he spoke, praising God.
Fear came over everyone who lived around them, and throughout the hill country of Judea people were talking about all these things.
Everyone who heard kept these things in their hearts, saying, “What will this child become?” For the hand of the Lord was with him.
His father Zechariah was filled with the Holy Spirit and prophesied, saying:
“Blessed is the God of Israel, because he has visited his people and brought them redemption.
He has raised up a horn of salvation for us in the house of David his servant,
just as he spoke through the mouths of his holy prophets long ago,
Salvation from our enemies and from the hand of everyone who hates us.
to show mercy to our ancestors and remember his holy covenant,
the oath he swore to Abraham our father, to grant us
that, rescued from our enemies, we might serve him without fear,
in holiness and righteousness before him all our days.
And you, my child, will be called the prophet of the Most High, for you will go ahead of the Lord to prepare his ways,
to give his people knowledge of salvation through the forgiveness of their sins,
because of the tender mercy of our God, through which the light from on high will visit us,
to shine on those in darkness and those sitting in the shadow of death, and to guide our feet into the way of peace.”
The child grew and became strong in spirit. He lived in the wilderness until the day he appeared publicly to Israel.
In those days a decree went out from Emperor Augustus that the whole inhabited world should be registered according to its towns.
This was the first census, which took place when Quirinius was governor of Syria.
Everyone went to be registered, each to his own city.
Joseph also went up from Galilee, from the town of Nazareth, to Judea, to the city of David called Bethlehem, because he was from the house and family of David.
To register with Mary, who was engaged to him and was pregnant.
While they were there, the time came for her to give birth.
She gave birth to her firstborn son, wrapped him in strips of cloth, and laid him in a manger, because there was no room for them in the lodging place.
There were shepherds in that region staying out in the fields, keeping watch over their flock of sheep at night.
The angel of the Lord appeared to them, and the glory of the Lord shone on them. They were terribly afraid.
The angel said to them, “Do not be afraid. Look, I will announce to you good news of great joy that will be for all the people,
because today a Savior has been born for you in the city of David. He is Christ the Lord.
This will be a sign for you: you will find a child wrapped in strips of cloth and lying in a manger.”
Suddenly a multitude of the heavenly army appeared with the angel, praising God and saying,
“Glory to God in the highest places, and peace on earth among the people he favors.”
When the angels had gone away from them into heaven, the shepherds said to one another, “Let us go to Bethlehem and see this thing that has happened, which the Lord has made known to us.”
They hurried there and found Mary and Joseph, and the child lying in a manger.
When they saw him, they understood the message that had been told to them about the child.
Everyone who heard was amazed at what the shepherds told them.
Mary treasured all these words, keeping them in her heart.
The shepherds returned, glorifying and praising God for everything they had heard and seen, just as they had been told.
When eight days had passed and it was time to circumcise him, he was named Jesus, the name the angel had given him before she conceived him in the womb.
When the days of their purification according to the law of Moses were completed, they brought him up to Jerusalem to present him to the Lord,
as it is written in the law of the Lord: “Every male who opens the womb shall be called holy to the Lord,”
and to offer a sacrifice according to what is stated in the law of the Lord: “A pair of turtledoves or two young pigeons.”
Now there was a man in Jerusalem named Simeon. This man was righteous and devoted to God, waiting for the consolation of Israel, and the Holy Spirit was with him.
It had been revealed to him through the Holy Spirit that he would not die before he had seen the Lord’s Christ.
And he came into the temple under the guidance of the Spirit. When the parents brought in the child Jesus to do for him what was customary under the law,
he took him in his arms, blessed God, and said,
“Now, Lord, you will release your servant in peace, according to your word,
because my eyes have seen your salvation,
which you have prepared in the presence of all peoples:
a light for revelation to the nations and for the glory of your people Israel.”
His father and mother were amazed at what was being said about him.
Simeon blessed them and said to Mary his mother, “Look, this child is appointed for the fall and rise of many in Israel, and as a sign that will be spoken against.
And a sword will pass through your own soul, so that the thoughts of many hearts may be revealed.”
There was a prophetess named Anna, the daughter of Phanuel, from the tribe of Asher. She had grown very old, having lived with her husband for seven years after her maidenhood.
She remained a widow until she was eighty-four years old. She never left the temple, worshiping day and night with fasting and prayers.
At that very hour she came forward and gave thanks to the Lord. She spoke with everyone who was awaiting the redemption of Jerusalem.
When they had completed everything according to the law of the Lord, they returned to Galilee, to their own town of Nazareth.
The child grew and became strong, filled with wisdom, and God's grace was upon him.
His parents went to Jerusalem every year for the Passover festival.
When he was twelve years old, they were going up according to the custom of the festival.
When the days were over and they were returning, the child Jesus stayed behind in Jerusalem, but his parents did not know it.
They thought he was traveling with them. After traveling for a day, they looked for him among their relatives and acquaintances.
When they did not find him, they returned to Jerusalem, looking for him.
After three days they found him in the temple, sitting among the teachers, listening to them and asking them questions.
Everyone who heard him was amazed at his wisdom and his answers.
When they saw him, they were amazed. His mother said to him, “My son, why have you treated us this way? Look, your father and I have been anxiously looking for you.”
He said to them, “Why are you looking for me? Do you not know that I must be about my Father's affairs?”
But they did not understand what he had said to them.
He went down with them to Nazareth and was obedient to them. His mother kept all these words in her heart.
Jesus continued to grow in wisdom and maturity, and in favor with God and people.

In the fifteenth year of the reign of Tiberius Caesar, when Pontius Pilate was governor over Judea, Herod was tetrarch over Galilee, his brother Philip was tetrarch over Iturea and the region of Trachonitis, and Lysanias was tetrarch over Abilene,
during the high priesthood of Annas and Caiaphas, the word of God came to John, the son of Zechariah, in the wilderness.
He went throughout the whole region around the Jordan, preaching a baptism of repentance for the forgiveness of sins,
as it is written in the book of the words of Isaiah the prophet: “The voice of one crying out in the wilderness: ‘Prepare the way of the Lord; make his paths straight.
Every valley will be filled, and every mountain and hill will be brought low. The crooked places will become straight, and the rough places will become smooth roads.
The glory of the Lord will be revealed, and all flesh will see the salvation of God.’”
He therefore said to the crowds coming to be baptized by him, “You brood of vipers! Who warned you to flee from the coming wrath?
Produce fruit worthy of your repentance, and do not begin saying to yourselves, ‘We have Abraham as our father.’ For I tell you that God is able to raise up children for Abraham from these stones.”
Even now the ax lies at the root of the trees. Every tree that does not produce good fruit will be cut down and thrown into the fire.
The crowds asked him, “What, then, should we do so that we may live?”
He answered them, “Whoever has two tunics should give one to someone who has none, and whoever has bread should do the same.”
Some tax collectors also came to be baptized by him and said to him, “Teacher, what should we do?”
He said to them, “Do not collect anything beyond what has been assigned to you.”
Soldiers also asked him, “And what should we do?” He said to them, “Do not extort anything from anyone or falsely accuse anyone, and be content with your pay.”
The people were waiting expectantly, and all were wondering in their hearts about John, whether he might be the Christ.
John answered everyone, “I baptize you with water, but someone stronger than I am is coming. I am not worthy to untie the strap of his sandal. He will baptize you with the Holy Spirit and fire.
His winnowing shovel is in his hand to clear his threshing floor and gather his wheat into his storehouse, but he will burn the chaff with a fire that cannot be put out.”
With many other words he urged them and preached to the people.
But Herod the tetrarch was rebuked by him because of Herodias, the wife of his brother Philip, and because of all the evil things Herod had done.
He added this to all his other deeds: he locked John in prison.
When all the people were being baptized, Jesus also received baptism and prayed, and heaven opened.
The Holy Spirit came down upon him in bodily form like a dove, and a voice came from heaven: “You are my beloved Son; I am pleased with you.”
Jesus was thirty years old. He was, as people supposed, the son of Joseph, the son of Heli,
the son of Matthat, the son of Levi, the son of Melchi, the son of Jannai, the son of Joseph,
the son of Mattathias, the son of Amos, the son of Nahum, the son of Nesli, the son of Aggai,
the son of Maath, the son of Mattathias, the son of Semein, the son of Josech, the son of Joda,
the son of Joanan, the son of Rhesa, the son of Zerubbabel, the son of Shealtiel, the son of Neri.
The son of Melchi, the son of Addi, the son of Cosam, the son of Elmadam, the son of Neri.
The son of Joshua, the son of Eliezer, the son of Jorim, the son of Matthat, the son of Levi.
The son of Simeon, the son of Judah, the son of Joseph, the son of Jonam, the son of Eliakim.
The son of Melea, the son of Menna, the son of Mattatha, the son of Nathan, the son of David.
The son of Jesse, the son of Obed, the son of Boaz, the son of Sala, the son of Nahshon.
The son of Adam, the son of Admin, the son of Arni, the son of Hezron, the son of Perez, the son of Judah.
The son of Jacob, the son of Isaac, the son of Abraham, the son of Terah, the son of Nahor.
The son of Serug, the son of Reu, the son of Peleg, the son of Eber, the son of Shelah.
The son of Cainan, the son of Arphaxad, the son of Shem, the son of Noah, the son of Lamech.
The son of Methuselah, the son of Enoch, the son of Jared, the son of Mahalalel, the son of Cainan.
The son of Enosh, the son of Seth, the son of Adam, the son of God.
Jesus, full of the Holy Spirit, returned from the Jordan and traveled in the wilderness in the Spirit.
For forty days he was tempted by the devil. He ate nothing during those days, and when they were over, he was hungry.
The devil said to him, “If you are the Son of God, tell this stone to become bread.”
Jesus answered him, “It is written: ‘A person will not live on bread alone.’”
He took him up and showed him all the kingdoms of the inhabited world in a moment.
The devil said to him, “I will give you all this authority and their glory, because it has been handed over to me, and I give it to whomever I wish.
So if you bow down in worship before me, it will all be yours.”
Jesus answered him, “It is written: ‘You shall worship the Lord your God and serve him alone.’”
He brought him to Jerusalem and made him stand on the pinnacle of the temple. He said to him, “If you are the Son of God, throw yourself down from here.
For it is written: ‘He will command his angels concerning you to protect you,’
and ‘They will lift you up in their hands so that you do not strike your foot against a stone.’”
Jesus answered him, “It has been said: ‘You shall not put the Lord your God to the test.’”
When the devil had finished every temptation, he withdrew from him for a time.
Jesus returned to Galilee in the power of the Spirit, and news about him spread throughout the surrounding region.
He was teaching in their synagogues, and everyone praised him.
He came to Nazareth, where he had been brought up. As was his custom, he went into the synagogue on the Sabbath days, and he stood up to read.
He was given the book of the prophet Isaiah. He opened the book and found the place where it was written:

“The Spirit of the Lord is upon me. Because of this, he has anointed me and sent me to bring good news to the poor, to proclaim release to captives and restored sight to the blind, and to set the oppressed free,
and to proclaim the year of the Lord’s favor.”
Then he rolled up the scroll, gave it to the attendant, and sat down. Everyone in the synagogue had their eyes fixed on him.
He began to say to them, “Today this scripture has been fulfilled in your hearing.”
Everyone spoke well of him and marveled at the gracious words coming from his mouth. They said, “Isn’t this Joseph’s son?”
He said to them, “You will certainly quote this proverb to me: ‘Doctor, heal yourself!’ Do here in your hometown the things we have heard happened in Capernaum.”
Then he said, “Truly I tell you, no prophet is accepted in his own hometown.
But I tell you the truth: there were many widows in Israel in the days of Elijah, when the sky was shut for three years and six months and a great famine came over the whole land.
Yet Elijah was not sent to any of them, but only to a widow in Zarephath in the region of Sidon.
And there were many people with leprosy in Israel in the time of the prophet Elisha, but none of them was cleansed except Naaman the Syrian.”
Everyone in the synagogue was filled with anger when they heard these things.
They got up, drove him out of the city, and took him to the edge of the hill on which their city was built, intending to throw him down headfirst.
But he passed through their midst and went away.
Then he went down to Capernaum, a city in Galilee, and taught on the Sabbaths.
They were all amazed at his teaching, because he spoke with authority.
In the synagogue there was a man who had the spirit of an unclean demon in him. He cried out in a loud voice,
“What do you want with us, Jesus of Nazareth? Have you come to destroy us? I know who you are: you are the Holy One of God!”
Jesus rebuked him, saying, “Be quiet and come out of him!” The demon threw the man down in their midst and came out of him without harming him at all.
Amazement came over everyone, and they said to one another, “What is this word? With authority and power he commands the unclean spirits, and they come out!”
News about him spread everywhere in the surrounding region.
Then he got up, left the synagogue, and entered Simon’s house. Simon’s mother-in-law had a high fever, and they pleaded with him on her behalf.
He stood over her and rebuked the fever, and it left her. Immediately she got up and served them.
As the sun was setting, everyone who had people sick with various diseases brought them to him. He laid his hand on each one of them and healed them.
Demons also came out of many people, shouting, “You are the Son of God!” But he rebuked them and would not let them speak, because they knew that he was the Christ.
When daybreak came, he went out to a deserted place. The crowds were looking for him, and they came to him and tried to keep him from leaving them.
But he said to them, “I must also proclaim the good news of the kingdom of God to the other cities, because I was sent for this purpose.”
And he was preaching in the synagogues of Judea.
While the crowds were pressing around him and listening to the word of God, he was standing beside the lake of Gennesaret.
He saw two boats moored beside the lake. The fishermen had gotten out of them and were washing their nets.
He got into one of the boats, which belonged to Simon, and told him to put out a little from the shore. Then he sat down in the boat and taught the crowds.
When he had finished speaking, he said to Simon, “Go out into the deep water and let down the nets for a catch.”
Simon answered him, “Master, we worked hard all night and caught nothing. But because you say so, I will let down the nets.”
When they did this, they gathered a great number of fish, and the nets were about to tear.
They signaled to their partners in the other boat to come and help them. They came and filled both boats, so that they began to sink.
When Simon Peter saw this, he fell at Jesus’ feet and said, “Go away from me, Lord, because I am a sinful man.”
For fear had seized him and everyone with him because of the catch of fish they had taken.
The same was true of James and John, the sons of Zebedee, who were Simon’s partners. Jesus said to Simon, “Do not be afraid, for from now on you will be catching people.”
They brought the boats to shore, left everything behind, and followed him.
While he was in one of the cities, there was a man covered with leprosy. When he saw Jesus, he fell facedown before him and begged him, saying, “Lord, if you are willing, you can make me clean.”
He stretched out his hand and touched him, saying, “I am willing. Be clean.” Immediately the leprosy left him.
He commanded him, “Do not tell anyone, but go and show yourself to the priest, and make an offering for your cleansing as Moses commanded, as a testimony to them.”
The news about him was spreading, and crowds were gathering to listen to him and to be healed of their illnesses.
But he would withdraw to deserted places and pray.

One day, while he was teaching, Pharisees and teachers of the law were sitting there. They had come from every village of Galilee and Judea, and from Jerusalem. The power of the Lord was present for him to heal.
Some men were carrying a paralyzed man on a bed, and they were trying to bring him inside and place him before him.

Because of the crowd, they could not find a way to bring him inside. So they went up onto the roof and lowered him through the tiles, along with his bed, into the middle of the crowd, in front of Jesus.
When he saw their faith, he said, “Man, your sins are forgiven.”
The scribes and Pharisees began to reason among themselves, saying, “Who is this who speaks blasphemy? Who can forgive sins except God alone?”
When Jesus understood their thoughts, he said to them, “Why are you thinking these things in your hearts?”
“For which is easier: to say, ‘Your sins are forgiven,’ or to say, ‘Get up and walk’?”
“So that you may know that the Son of Man has authority on earth to forgive sins”—he said to the paralyzed man, “I tell you, get up, pick up your mat, and go home.”
Immediately he stood up in front of them, picked up his bed, and went home, giving glory to God.
They were all amazed and gave glory to God. They were filled with fear and said, “We have seen wonderful things today.”
After this, he went out and saw a tax collector named Levi sitting at his tax booth. He said to him, “Follow me.”
He left everything behind, got up, and followed him.
Levi gave a great banquet for him in his house. A large crowd of tax collectors and others were reclining at the meal with them.
The Pharisees and the scribes complained to his disciples, saying, “Why do you eat and drink with tax collectors and sinners?”
Jesus answered them, “Healthy people do not need a doctor, but those who are sick do.
I have not come to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.”
They said to him, “John’s disciples often fast and pray, and so do those of the Pharisees, but yours eat and drink.”
Jesus said to them, “Can you make the wedding guests fast while the bridegroom is with them?”
But days are coming when the bridegroom will be taken away from them. Then they will fast in those days.

He also told them another parable: “No one tears a patch from a new garment and attaches it to an old garment. Otherwise, he will tear the new garment too, and the new patch will not match the old one.
And no one puts new wine into old wineskins. Otherwise, the new wine will burst the wineskins and spill out, and the wineskins will also be ruined.
Instead, new wine is put into new wineskins.
No one who drinks old wine wants new wine, for he says, ‘The old wine is good.’”
On the Sabbath, he was going through the grainfields. His disciples picked the heads of grain, rubbed them in their hands, and ate.
Some of the Pharisees said, “Why are you doing what is not permitted on the Sabbath?”
Jesus answered them, “Have you not read what David did when he and those with him were hungry?
How he entered the house of God, took the bread set out before God, ate it, and gave it to those with him—bread that no one is permitted to eat except the priests alone?”
He said to them, “The Son of Man is Lord even of the Sabbath.”
On another Sabbath, he entered the synagogue and taught. There was a man there whose right hand was withered.
The scribes and the Pharisees were watching him closely to see whether he would heal him on the Sabbath, so that they could find a way to accuse him.
But he knew their thoughts and said to the man whose hand was withered, “Get up and stand in the middle.” He got up and stood there.
Jesus said to them, “I will ask you: Is it permitted on the Sabbath to do good or to do evil, to save a life or to destroy it?”
He looked around at all of them and said to him, “Stretch out your hand.” He stretched it out, and his hand was healed.
But they were filled with foolishness and discussed with one another, “What shall we do to Jesus?”
In those days he went out to the mountain to pray, and he stayed awake all night in prayer to God.
When morning came, he called his disciples and chose twelve from among them, whom he also named apostles.
Simon, who was named Peter, and his brother Andrew; James and his brother John; Philip and Bartholomew.
And Matthew, and Thomas, and James the son of Alphaeus, and Simon who was called the Zealot.
And Judas the son of James, and Judas Iscariot, who became a traitor.
He came down with them and stood in an open place, with a large crowd together with his disciples and a great crowd of people from Judea, Jerusalem, and the coastal region of Tyre and Sidon.
These had come to hear him and to be healed of their diseases. Those who were tormented by unclean spirits were also healed.
The whole crowd was trying to touch him, because power was coming out of him and healing them all.
He looked up at his disciples and said, “Blessed are the poor, because the kingdom of heaven is theirs.
Blessed are you who are hungry now, because you will be satisfied. Blessed are those who weep now, because they will laugh.
Blessed are you when people hate you, exclude you, insult you, and reject your name as evil because of the Son of Man.
Rejoice on that day and be glad! Look, your reward will be great in heaven, for their ancestors used to treat the prophets this way.
But woe to you who are rich, because you have received your comfort.
Woe to you who are full now, because you will be hungry. Woe to you who laugh now, because you will mourn and weep.
Woe to you when everyone honors you, for they used to treat the false prophets this way.
But I say to you who listen to me: Love your enemies. Do good to those who hate you.
Bless those who curse you. Pray for those who persecute you.
If someone strikes you on your cheek, turn the other one toward him too. And let the person who takes your cloak have your tunic as well.
Give to everyone who asks you, and do not demand your belongings back from someone who takes them.
And just as you want people to treat you, treat them that way yourselves.
And if you love those who love you, what credit is that to you? For even sinners love those who love them.
And if you do good to those who do good to you, what credit is that to you? Sinners also do this.
If you lend to those from whom you expect to receive repayment, what credit is that to you? Sinners also lend to sinners so that they may receive an equivalent amount back.

But love your enemies, do good, and lend without expecting to receive anything back. Your reward will be great, and you will become children of the Most High, because he is kind to the ungrateful and the wicked.
Be merciful, because your Father is merciful.
Do not judge, so that you will not be judged. Do not condemn, so that you will not be condemned. Forgive, and you will be forgiven.
Give, and you will be given a good measure, pressed down, shaken together, and overflowing. It will be poured into your lap. For the measure you use will be used to measure out to you.
He also told them another parable: “Can a blind person guide a blind person? Will they not both fall into a pit?
No student is above his teacher. Let everyone be fully trained, like his teacher.
Why do you look at the speck in your brother’s eye but do not see the beam in your own eye?

Or how can you say to your brother, ‘My brother, let me take the speck out of your eye,’ when you do not see the beam in your own eye? Hypocrite! First take the beam out of your own eye, and then you will see clearly to take the speck out of your brother’s eye.
For no good tree produces bad fruit, nor does a bad tree produce good fruit.
For each tree is known by its fruit. People do not gather figs from thorn bushes or harvest grapes from a bramble.
A good person brings out good things from the good store in his heart, and an evil person brings out evil things from his evil store. For the mouth speaks from what fills the heart.
Why do you call me ‘Lord, Lord,’ but do not do what I say?
Everyone who comes to me, hears my words, and acts on them—I will show you whom he is like.
He is like a man building a house who dug down deep and laid the foundation on rock. When the flood came, the river struck that house but could not overpower it, because it was well built.

But the person who hears them and does not act on them is like a man who built his house on the ground without a foundation. As soon as the river struck it, it fell, and the collapse of that house was great.
When he had finished speaking all his words in the hearing of the people, he entered Capernaum.
A centurion’s servant was sick and about to die. The centurion valued him highly.
When he heard about Jesus, he sent some Jewish elders to him, asking him to come and save his servant.
They came to Jesus and pleaded with him earnestly, saying, ‘He is worthy of your doing this for him.’
For he loves our nation, and he is the one who built the synagogue for us.
Jesus went with them. Before he reached the house, the centurion sent his friends to say to him, ‘Lord, do not trouble yourself, for I am not worthy to have you come under my roof.’
‘That is why I did not consider myself worthy to come to you. But just say the word: let my servant recover.’
‘For I too am a man under authority, with soldiers under me. I say to this one, “Go,” and he goes, and to another, “Come,” and he comes, and to my servant, “Do this,” and he does it.’
When Jesus heard these things, he marveled at him. He turned to those following him and said to them, ‘I tell you, I have not found such great faith even in Israel.’
Those who had been sent returned to the house and found that the servant had recovered.
Afterward, he went to a town called Nain. His disciples and a large crowd were walking with him.
As he approached the town gate, a dead man was being carried out, his mother’s only son. She was a widow, and a crowd from the town was with her.
When the Lord saw her, he had compassion on her and said to her, ‘Do not weep.’
He went forward and touched the bier, and those carrying it stopped. He said to him, ‘Young man, I tell you, get up!’
The dead man sat up and began to speak, and he gave him to his mother.
Fear seized them all, and they glorified God, saying, ‘A great prophet has arisen among us,’ and, ‘God has visited his people.’
The news about him spread throughout Judea and the whole surrounding region.
John’s disciples told him about all these things. John called two of his disciples.
He sent them to the Lord, saying, ‘Are you the one who is coming, or should we wait for someone else?’
When the men came to him, they said to him, ‘John the Baptist sent us to you to ask, “Are you the one who is coming, or should we wait for someone else?”’
At that time he had healed many people of their illnesses and afflictions and freed them from evil spirits, and he had granted sight to many blind people.

He answered them, ‘Go and report to John what you have seen and heard: blind people see, lame people walk, people with leprosy are cleansed, deaf people hear, dead people rise, and poor people are told the good news.’
And blessed is anyone who does not stumble because of me.
When John's messengers had gone, he began to speak to the crowds about John: “What did you go out into the wilderness to see? A reed shaken by the wind?
But what did you go out to see? A man dressed in soft clothes? Look, those who wear splendid clothes and live in luxury are in kings' houses.
But what did you go out to see? A prophet? Yes, I tell you, he is more than a prophet.
This is the one about whom it is written: ‘Look, I will send my messenger ahead of you, who will make your path straight before you.’
I tell you, among those born of women there is no one greater than John. Yet the one who is less than he is greater than he in the kingdom of God.
When all the people and the tax collectors heard this, they honored God, because they had received John's baptism.
But the Pharisees and the experts in the law rejected God's purpose, since they had not been baptized by him.
To whom, then, shall I compare the people of this generation? And whom are they like?
They are like little children sitting in the marketplace, calling to their companions and saying, ‘We played music for you, and you did not dance. We sang a lament, and you did not weep.’
For John the Baptist came neither eating bread nor drinking wine, and you said, ‘He has a demon.’
The Son of Man came eating and drinking, and you said, ‘Look, a glutton and a wine drinker, a friend of tax collectors and sinners!’
Wisdom has been shown to be right by all her children.
One of the Pharisees asked him to eat with him. He went into the Pharisee's house and reclined at the table.
Now there was a woman in the city who was a sinner. When she learned that he was reclining at the table in the Pharisee’s house, she brought an alabaster jar of perfumed ointment.
She stood behind him at his feet, weeping, and began to wet his feet with her tears. She wiped them with the hair of her head and kept kissing his feet and anointing them with perfume.
When the Pharisee who had invited him saw this, he said to himself, “If this man were a prophet, he would know who and what kind of woman is touching him—that she is a sinner.”
Jesus answered him, “Simon, I have something to say to you.” He said, “Teacher, say it.”
A moneylender had two debtors. One owed him five hundred staters, and the other fifty.
Since they had nothing with which to repay him, he forgave the debt of both. Which of them, then, will love him more?
Simon answered, “I suppose the one whose larger debt he forgave.” He said to him, “You have judged correctly.”
He turned toward the woman and said to Simon, “Do you see this woman? I came into your house, and you gave me no water for my feet. But she wet my feet with her tears and wiped them with her hair.
You gave me no kiss, but from the time I came in, she has not stopped kissing my feet.
You did not anoint my head with oil, but she anointed my feet with perfume.
For this reason I tell you, her many sins are forgiven, because she loved greatly. But the one who is forgiven little loves little.”
He said to her, “Your sins are forgiven.”
Those reclining at the table with him began to say to themselves, “Who is this who forgives sins?”
He said to the woman, “Your faith has saved you. Go in peace.”
After this, he traveled through cities and villages, preaching and announcing the good news of the kingdom of God. The twelve were with him,
along with some women whom he had healed of evil spirits and illnesses: Mary, called Magdalene, from whom seven demons had come out,
and Joanna, the wife of Chuza, Herod’s steward, and Susanna, and many others who provided for him out of their own resources.
As a large crowd gathered, along with people coming to him from the cities, he spoke to them in a parable:
“A sower went out to sow his seed. As he sowed, some fell beside the road and were trampled, and the birds of the sky ate them.
Other seeds fell on the rock, and when they sprouted, they dried up because there was no moisture beneath them.
Other seeds fell among the thorns, and when the thorns grew, they choked them.
Other seeds fell on good soil, and when they grew, they produced a hundredfold crop.” As he said these things, he called out, “Whoever has ears to hear, let them hear!”
His disciples asked him, “What does this parable mean?”

He said to them, “You have been granted understanding of the mystery of the kingdom of God. But I speak to the rest in parables, so that though they see, they may not perceive, and though they hear, they may not understand.
This is the meaning of the parable: the seed is the word of God.
Those beside the road are those who have heard. Then the evil one comes and takes the word out of their hearts, so that they may not believe and be saved.
Those on the rock are those who hear and receive the word with joy. But they have no root. They believe for a time, but in a time of testing they turn away.
Those that fell among the thorns are those who hear the word, but as they go through life, they are choked by its worries, riches, and pleasures, and do not reach maturity.
Those on the good soil are those who have heard the word with a noble and good heart, hold on to it, and bear fruit with perseverance.
No one lights a lamp and covers it with a vessel or puts it under a bed. Instead, they put it on a lampstand so that those who enter can see the light.
For nothing is hidden that will not be revealed, and nothing is concealed that will not be known and come to light.
So pay attention to how you listen. For whoever has will be given more, and whoever does not have will have even what they say they have taken away from them.”
His mother and his brothers came to him, but they could not reach him because of the crowd.
He was told, “Your mother and your brothers are standing outside, wanting to see you.”
He answered them, “My mother and my brothers are those who hear the word of God and do it.”
One day he got into a boat with his disciples and said to them, “Let us go to the other side of the lake.” And they set sail.
As they sailed, he fell asleep. A windstorm came down on the lake, and they were thrown into turmoil and were in danger.
They approached him and woke him, saying, “Master, Master, we are going to perish!” He got up and rebuked the wind and the waves of the water. It stopped, and there was a calm.
He said to them, “Where is your faith?” Frightened and amazed, they said to one another, “Who, then, is this? He commands the winds and the water, and they obey him!”
They sailed to the region of the Gerasenes, which is opposite Galilee.
When he came ashore, a man coming from the town met him. He had demons in him and had worn no clothes for a long time. He did not live in a house but among the tombs.
When he saw Jesus, he cried out and fell down before him, saying in a loud voice, “What do you want with us, Jesus, Son of the Most High God? I beg you, do not torment me!”

For he had commanded the unclean spirits to come out of the man. For a long time it had been seizing him. He would be bound with chains and bronze shackles and kept under guard, but he would break the bonds and be driven by the demon into deserted places.
Jesus asked him, “What is your name?” He said, “Legion,” because many demons had entered him.
They begged him not to command them to go into the abyss.
There was a large herd of pigs there, being tended on the mountain. They begged him to command them to enter those pigs, and he allowed them.
The demons came out of the man and entered the pigs. The herd rushed down the steep slope into the lake, and they died.
When the herders saw what had happened, they fled and reported it in the town and in the countryside.

The people came out to see what had happened. They came to Jesus and found the man from whom the demons had come out sitting there, wearing his clothes and in his right mind, sitting at Jesus’ feet. They were afraid.
Those who had seen it told them how the demon-possessed man had been healed.
The whole crowd from the surrounding region of the Gerasenes begged him to leave them, because great fear had seized them. He got into a boat and returned.
The man from whom the demons had come out begged him to let him go with him. But he sent him away, saying:
“Return to your home and tell what God has done for you.” He went throughout the whole town, proclaiming what God had done for him.
When Jesus returned, the crowd welcomed him, for they had all been waiting for him.
Then a man named Jairus came. He was a leader of the synagogue. He fell at Jesus’ feet and begged him to come into his house.
For he had an only daughter, about twelve years old, who was dying. As he went, the crowd pressed around him.
There was a woman who had been bleeding for twelve years, whom no one had been able to heal.
She came up behind him and touched the fringe of his robe, and immediately her bleeding stopped.
Jesus said, “Who touched me?” When they all said, “It was not us,” Peter said to him, “Master, the crowds are surrounding you and pressing against you.”
But Jesus said, “Someone touched me, for I felt power go out from me.”

When the woman saw that what she had done was not hidden, she came trembling and fell down before him. In front of the whole crowd, she told him why she had touched him and how she had been healed immediately.
He said to her, “My daughter, your faith has saved you. Go in peace.”
While he was still speaking, someone came from the synagogue leader’s household and said, “Your daughter has died. Do not trouble the teacher any longer.”
Jesus heard this and said, “Do not be afraid. Only believe, and she will live.”
When he came to the house, he allowed no one to go in with him except Peter, John, James, and the little girl’s father and mother.
They were all weeping and mourning for her. But he said, “Do not weep, for she is not dead but asleep.”
They laughed at him, knowing that she had died.
But he sent everyone out, took her hand, and called out, saying, “Little girl, get up.”
Her spirit returned to her, and she got up immediately. He ordered them to give her something to eat.
Her parents were amazed, but he instructed them not to tell anyone what had happened.
He called the twelve and gave them power and authority over all demons and to cure diseases.
He sent them to proclaim the kingdom of God and to heal the sick.
He said to them, “Take nothing for the journey: no staff, no bag, no bread, no money, and do not wear two tunics.
Whatever house you enter, stay there and leave from there.
As for those who will not welcome you, when you leave that town, shake the dust off your feet against them as a testimony to them.”
They went out and traveled from village to village, proclaiming the good news and healing everywhere.
Herod the tetrarch heard about everything that was happening. He was perplexed because some were saying that John had risen from the dead,
while others were saying that Elijah had appeared, and still others that one of the ancient prophets had risen.
But Herod said, “I am the one who beheaded John. Who, then, is this about whom I hear these things?” And he was trying to see him.
The apostles returned and told him what they had done. He took them with him and withdrew privately to a town called Bethsaida.
But the crowds learned about it and followed him. He welcomed them and spoke with them about the kingdom of God, and he healed those who needed healing.

The day had begun to draw to a close. The twelve approached him and said, “Send the crowds away so that they can go to the surrounding villages and farms, find lodging, and find food, because they are in a deserted place.”
But he said to them, “You yourselves give them something to eat.” They said to him, “We have no more than five loaves here and two fish, unless we ourselves go and buy something to eat for all [?].”
For there were about five thousand men. He said to his disciples, “Have them sit down in groups of fifty.”
They did so and had everyone sit down.
He took the five loaves and the two fish, looked up to heaven, blessed them, broke them, and gave them to the disciples. They set them before the crowd.
They all ate and were satisfied, and they picked up twelve baskets of broken pieces left over from them.
While he was praying alone in a place, with his disciples with him, he asked them, “Who do the crowds say I am?”
They answered, “Some say John the Baptist, others Elijah, others Jeremiah, and still others that one of the ancient prophets has risen.”
He said to them, “But who do you say I am?” Peter answered, “You are the Christ of God.”
But he sternly warned him and commanded him, “Do not tell this to anyone.”
He said, “The Son of Man must suffer many things, be rejected by the elders, the chief priests, and the scribes, be killed, and rise on the third day.”
He said to everyone, “Anyone who wants to follow me must deny himself, take up his cross every day, and follow me.
For whoever wants to save his life will lose it, and whoever loses his life for my sake will save it.
For what will a person gain if he gains the whole world but loses or ruins himself?
For whoever is ashamed of me and my words, the Son of Man will be ashamed of him when he comes in his own glory and the glory of his Father and his holy angels.
But I tell you truly, some of those standing here will not taste death until they see the kingdom of God.”
About eight days after these words, he took Peter, John, and James and went up the mountain to pray.
While he was praying, the appearance of his face changed, and his clothing became white and dazzling.
And look, two men were talking with him. They were Moses and Elijah.
They appeared in glory and spoke about his departure, which he was going to accomplish in Jerusalem.
Peter and those with him were weighed down with sleep. But when they became fully awake, they saw his glory and the two men standing with him.
As they were leaving him, Peter said to Jesus, “Master, it is good for us to be here. Let us make three shelters: one for you, one for Moses, and one for Elijah.” He did not know what he was saying.
While he was saying these things, a cloud appeared and overshadowed them. They became afraid as those men entered the cloud.
A voice came from the cloud, saying, “This is my chosen Son. Listen to him.” As [?]
When the voice came, they found Jesus alone. They kept silent and told no one in those days about anything they had seen.
The next day, as they were coming down from the mountain, a large crowd met him.
And look, a man from the crowd cried out, “Teacher, I beg you, look at my son, because he is my only child.
Look, a spirit seizes him, and he suddenly cries out. It throws him into convulsions, and he foams at the mouth. It hardly ever leaves him, tormenting him.
I begged your disciples to cast it out, but they could not.”
Jesus answered, “You unbelieving and perverse generation! How long will I be with you? How long will I put up with you? Bring your son here to me.”
While the boy was still approaching him, the demon threw him down and sent him into convulsions. But Jesus rebuked the unclean spirit, healed the boy, and gave him back to his father.
They were all amazed at the greatness of God. While they were all marveling at the things he was doing, he said to his disciples,
“Take all these words to heart, for the Son of Man will be handed over into human hands.”
But they did not understand this saying. It was hidden from them so that they would not understand it, and they were afraid to ask him about this saying.
A thought arose among them about who was the greatest among them.
But Jesus, knowing the thoughts in their hearts, took a little child and stood him beside him.
He said to them, “Whoever welcomes this little child in my name welcomes me, and whoever welcomes me welcomes the one who sent me. The least among all of you is the greatest.”
John answered, “Master, we saw someone casting out demons in your name, and we stopped him because he does not follow you with us.”
Jesus said to him, “Do not stop him, for whoever is not against you is for you.”
As the days approached for him to be taken up, he firmly resolved to go to Jerusalem.
He sent messengers ahead of him. As they traveled, they entered a Samaritan village to make preparations for him.
But they did not welcome him, because he was heading toward Jerusalem.
When the disciples James and John saw this, they said to him, “Lord, do you want us to command fire to come down from heaven and destroy them?”
But he turned and rebuked them.
He went to another village.
As they were traveling along the road, someone said to him, “I will follow you wherever you go.” Jesus said to him,
“Foxes have dens, and the birds of the sky have nests, but the Son of Man has nowhere to lay his head.”
He said to another person, “Follow me.” But he said, “Lord, let me first go and bury my father.”
He said to him, “Leave the dead to bury their own dead. But you go and proclaim the kingdom of God.”
Another person said, “I will follow you, Lord, but first let me go and say goodbye to those in my household.”
Jesus said, “No one who puts his hand to a plow and looks back is fit for the kingdom of God.”
After this, the Lord chose seventy-two others and sent them ahead of him in pairs to every city and place he was going to enter.
He said to them, “The harvest is plentiful, but the workers are few. So plead with the Lord of the harvest to send workers out into his harvest.
Go! Look, I am sending you like lambs among wolves.
Do not carry a money pouch, a bag, or sandals, and do not greet anyone along the road.
Whatever house you enter, first say, ‘Peace to this house.’
If a person of peace is there, your peace will rest on him. But if not, it will return to you.
Stay in the same house, eating and drinking what they provide, for the worker deserves his wages. Do not move from house to house.
Whatever city you enter, if they welcome you, eat what is set before you.
Heal the sick there and tell them, ‘The kingdom of God has come near to you.’
But whatever city you enter, if they do not welcome you, go out into its streets and say,
‘Even the dust from your city that has stuck to our feet, we wipe off against you. Nevertheless, know this: the kingdom of God has come near to you.’
I tell you, it will be more bearable for Sodom on that day than for that city.
Woe to you, Chorazin! Woe to you, Bethsaida! For if the miracles that took place among you had taken place in Tyre and Sidon, they would have sat in sackcloth and ashes and repented.
But it will be more bearable for Tyre and Sidon at the judgment than for you.
And you, Capernaum, will you be lifted up to heaven? You will be brought down to Hades.
Whoever listens to you listens to me, and whoever rejects you rejects me. And whoever rejects me rejects the one who sent me.
The seventy-two returned with joy, saying, “Lord, even the demons submit to us in your name!”
He said to them, “I was watching Satan fall from heaven like lightning.”
Look, I have given you authority to tread on snakes and scorpions and over all the enemy’s power, and nothing will harm you.
But do not rejoice because the spirits submit to you. Instead, rejoice because your names are written in heaven.

At that moment he rejoiced in the Holy Spirit and said, “I praise you, my Father, Lord of heaven and earth, because you have hidden these things from the wise and intelligent and revealed them to little children. Yes, my Father, because this is what pleased you.”
Everything has been given to me by my Father. No one knows who the Son is except the Father, or who the Father is except the Son and anyone to whom the Son chooses to reveal him.
He turned to the disciples and said to them privately, “Blessed are the eyes that see what you see!”
For I tell you, many prophets and kings wanted to see what you see, but did not see it, and to hear me [?] what you hear, but did not hear it.
Then a legal expert stood up to test him, saying, “Teacher, what must I do to inherit eternal life?”
He said, “What is written in the law? How do you read it?”
He answered, “You must love the Lord your God with all your heart, all your soul, all your strength, and all your thoughts, and your neighbor as yourself.”
He said to him, “You have answered correctly. Do this, and you will live.”
But wanting to justify himself, he said to Jesus, “Who is my neighbor?”
Jesus answered him, “A man was traveling from Jerusalem to Jericho and fell into the hands of robbers. They stripped him, wounded him, and went away, leaving him half dead.”
By chance, a priest was going down that road. He saw him and passed by on the other side.
Likewise, a Levite came to that place, saw him, and passed by on the other side.
But a Samaritan who was traveling came upon him. When he saw him, he had compassion on him.
He went up to him, bandaged his wounds, and poured oil and wine on them. He put him on his own animal, brought him to an inn, and took care of him.
The next day, as he was leaving, he gave two silver coins to the innkeeper and said to him, “Take care of him. Whatever more you spend on him, I will repay you when I return.”
Which of these three, in your opinion, became a neighbor to the man who fell into the hands of the robbers?
He said to him, “The one who showed him mercy.” Jesus said to him, “Go and do the same yourself.”
As they were traveling, he entered a village, and a woman named Martha welcomed him.
She had a sister called Mary, who sat at the Lord’s feet and listened to his word.
But Martha was distracted by all the serving she had to do. She came up to him and said, “Lord, don’t you care that my sister has left me to serve alone? Tell her, then, to help me.”
The Lord answered her, “Martha, Martha, you are worried about many things and are troubled.
But only one thing is needed. For Mary has chosen the good portion for herself, and it will not be taken away from her.”
He was praying in a certain place. When he finished, one of his disciples said to him, “Lord, teach us to pray, just as John taught his disciples.”
He said to them, “When you pray, say: ‘Our Father in heaven, may your name be held holy. May your kingdom come. May your will be done.
Give us each day our bread for the coming day.
Forgive us our sins, for we too forgive everyone who owes us. And do not lead us into temptation.’”
He said to them, “Which of you has a friend and will go to him at midnight and say to him, ‘Friend, lend me three loaves of bread,
because a friend has come to me from a journey, and I have nothing to set before him’?
And the one inside answers, ‘Do not trouble me. I have already shut my door, and my children are in bed with me. I cannot get up to give you anything.’
I tell you, even if he will not get up and give him anything because he is his friend, he will nevertheless get up because of his shameless persistence and give him whatever he needs.
I too tell you: ask, and you will be given; seek, and you will find; knock, and the door will be opened to you.
For everyone who asks will receive, and whoever seeks will find, and whoever knocks will have the door opened to him.
Which of you, if his son asks him for a fish, will give him a snake instead of a fish?
Or if he asks him for an egg, will he give him a scorpion?
So if you, though you are evil, know how to give good things to your children, how much more will your Father give the Holy Spirit from heaven to those who ask him!”
He was driving out a demon that could not speak. When the demon came out, the man who had been unable to speak spoke, and the crowds were amazed.
But some of them said, “He drives out demons by Beelzebul, the ruler of the demons.”
Others, testing him, were asking him for a sign from heaven.
But he knew the thoughts in their hearts and said to them, “Every kingdom divided against itself becomes desolate, and one house falls upon another.
If Satan too is divided against himself, how will his kingdom stand? For you say that I drive out demons by Beelzebul.
If I drive out demons by Beelzebul, by whom do your sons drive them out? Therefore they will be your judges.
But if I drive out demons by the finger of God, then the kingdom of God has come upon you.
When a strong man guards his courtyard, fully armed, all his possessions are safe.
But when someone stronger than he is comes and overcomes him, he will take away all the armor in which he trusted and divide up his plunder.
Whoever is not with me is against me, and whoever does not gather with me scatters.
When an unclean spirit comes out of a person, it travels through places without water, looking for a place to rest. When it finds none, it says, “I will return to my house, the place I came out of.”
When it arrives, it finds the house swept and put in order.
Then it goes and takes seven other spirits more evil than itself. They enter and live there, and that person's final condition becomes worse than the first.
As he was saying these things, a woman in the crowd raised her voice and said to him, “Blessed is the womb that carried you and the breasts that you nursed from!”
But he said, “Rather, blessed are those who hear the word of God and keep it.”
As a crowd gathered around him, he began to say, “This generation is an evil generation. It looks for a sign, but no sign will be given to it except the sign of Jonah.”
For just as Jonah became a sign to the people of Nineveh, so the Son of Man will be to this generation.

The queen of the South will rise on the day of judgment with the people of this generation and condemn them, because she came from the ends of the earth to hear Solomon's wisdom. And look, someone greater than Solomon is here.
The people of Nineveh will rise at the judgment with this generation and condemn it, because they repented at Jonah's preaching. Look, someone greater than Jonah is here.
No one lights a lamp and puts it in a hidden place. Instead, they put it on the lampstand so that those who enter can see the light.
The eye is the lamp of the body. If your eye is sound, your whole body is full of light. But if your eye is bad, your whole body will be dark.
So take care that the light within you is not darkness.
If, then, your whole body is full of light, with no dark part in it, it will be entirely full of light, just as a lamp shines on you with its brightness.
While he was speaking, a Pharisee asked him to eat with him. He went inside and reclined at the table.
When the Pharisee saw this, he was surprised that he had not first washed before eating.
But the Lord said to him, “Now you Pharisees clean the outside of the cup and the dish, but your inside is full of robbery and uncleanness. You fools!”
Did not the one who made the outside also make the inside?
But give alms as things are, and look, everything is clean for you.
But woe to you Pharisees, because you give a tenth of mint, rue, and every herb, but neglect justice and the love of God. You ought to do these things without neglecting the others.
Woe to you Pharisees, because you love the seats of honor in the synagogues and greetings in the marketplaces.
Woe to you, because you are like unmarked graves that people walk over without knowing it.
One of the experts in the law answered him, “Teacher, by saying these things, you insult us too.”
But he said to them, “Woe to you experts in the law too, because you load people with burdens that are hard to carry, but you yourselves do not touch the burdens with one of your fingers.”
Woe to you, because you build the tombs of the prophets, but your ancestors were the ones who killed them.
So you bear witness to and approve of your ancestors' deeds, because they killed them, while you do the building.
For this reason the wisdom of God also said, “I will send them prophets and apostles, and they will kill some of them and persecute others.”
so that this generation will be held accountable for the blood of all the prophets shed since the foundation of the world,
from the blood of Abel to the blood of Zechariah son of Berechiah, whom they killed between the altar and the temple. Yes, I tell you, this generation will be held accountable for it.
Woe to you experts in the law, because you have taken away the key to knowledge! You did not enter yourselves, and you did not let those who were entering go in.
When he left that place, the scribes and the Pharisees began to press him to keep silent about many things.
About many things, they were laying traps for him, to catch him in something he said.

Meanwhile, as tens of thousands of people gathered, so that they were trampling one another, he began to speak first to his disciples: “Guard yourselves against the yeast, that is, the hypocrisy of the Pharisees.
Nothing is covered that will not be revealed, or hidden that will not become known.
Therefore, what you have said in the darkness will be heard in the light, and what you have whispered in people's ears in private rooms will be proclaimed from the rooftops.
I tell you, my friends, do not be afraid of those who kill your body and afterward can do nothing more to you.
But I will show you whom you should fear. Fear the one who, after killing you, has authority to throw you into Gehenna. Yes, I tell you, fear him.
Are not five sparrows sold for two obols? Yet not one of them is forgotten before God.
Even all the hairs of your head are counted. Do not be afraid; you are worth more than many sparrows.
I tell you, everyone who acknowledges me before people, the Son of Man will also acknowledge before the angels of God.
But whoever denies me before people will be denied before the angels of God.
Everyone who speaks a word against the Son of Man will be forgiven, but whoever blasphemes against the Holy Spirit will not be forgiven.
When they bring you before the synagogues, rulers, and authorities, do not worry about what you will say, how you will act, or how you will answer them.
For the Holy Spirit will teach you at that very hour what you should say.”
Someone from the crowd said to him, “Teacher, tell my brother to divide the inheritance between us.”
But he said, “Man, who appointed me as a judge or someone to divide property between you?”
He said to them, “Pay attention and guard yourselves against every kind of greed. If someone's possessions increase, will he find his life in them?”
He told them a parable, saying, “A rich man's land produced a plentiful harvest.
He thought to himself, ‘What shall I do? I have nowhere to gather my crops.’
Then he said, ‘I will do this: I will tear down my storehouses and build larger ones, and gather all the grain and my goods into them.
Then I will say to my soul, “My soul, you have many good things stored up for many years. Rest, eat, drink, and enjoy yourself.”’
But God said to him, ‘Fool! This very night your soul will be taken from you. Then who will own the things you have prepared?’
This is how it is with someone who stores up wealth for himself but is not rich in God.”
He said to his disciples, “Therefore I tell you: Do not worry about your life, what you will eat, or about your body, what you will put on.
For your life is more than food, and the body is more than clothing.
Look at the ravens: they neither sow nor reap, and they have neither a storeroom nor a barn, yet God feeds them. You are worth far more than the birds!
Which of you can add a cubit to his height by worrying?
So if you cannot do even a little thing, why do you worry about the rest?
Consider the lilies, how they grow: they neither toil nor spin. Yet I tell you that even Solomon in all his glory was not dressed like one of these.
If God clothes the grass this way, which is in the field today and will be thrown into the oven tomorrow, how much more will he clothe you, you of little faith!
You, too, must not seek what you will eat or what you will drink. Do not worry.
For the nations of the world seek all these things, but your Father knows that you need them.
Instead, seek his kingdom, and these things will be added to you.
Do not be afraid, little flock, because your Father wants to give you the kingdom.
Sell your possessions and give them as charity. Make yourselves purses that will not wear out, an inexhaustible treasure in heaven, where no thief approaches and no moth destroys.
For where your treasure will be, your heart will be there too.
Keep your waists belted and your lamps burning.
Be like people waiting for their master to return from the wedding feast, so that when he comes and knocks, they will open the door for him immediately.
Blessed are those slaves whose master finds them keeping watch when he comes. Truly I tell you that he will fasten his belt, have them recline at the table, and come to serve them.
Even if he comes during the second watch or the third and finds them doing this, blessed are those slaves.
Understand this: if the master of the house had known at what hour the thief was coming, he would not have allowed his house to be broken into.
You, too, must be ready, because the Son of Man is coming at an hour you do not know.”
Peter said to him, “Lord, are you telling this parable to us, or are you telling it to everyone?”
The Lord said, “Who, then, is the faithful and wise manager whom his master will put in charge of his slaves to give them their food at the proper time?
Blessed is that slave whom his master finds doing this when he comes.
Truly I tell you that he will put him in charge of all his possessions.
But if that slave says in his heart, ‘My master will be late in coming,’ and begins to beat the male and female slaves, and to eat, drink, and get drunk,
that slave’s master will come on a day he does not know and at an hour he is unaware of. He will cut him in two and assign him a place with the unfaithful.
The slave who knew his master’s will but did not prepare or act according to his will will receive many heavy blows.

But the one who did not know and did things deserving a beating will receive few lashes. Everyone who has been given much will have more required of him, and the one entrusted with much will be asked for much.
I came to cast fire on the earth, and how I wish it were burning!
I have a baptism to undergo, and I am distressed until it is completed.
Do you think that I came to bring peace to the earth? I tell you, no, but division.
For from now on, five people in one house will be divided, three against two and two against three.

A father will be divided against his son, and a son against his father; a mother against her daughter, and a daughter against her mother; a mother-in-law against her daughter-in-law, and a daughter-in-law against her mother-in-law.
He also said to the crowds, "When you see a cloud rising in the west, you immediately say, 'It will rain,' and that is what happens."
And when the south wind blows: 'There will be scorching heat,' and it happens.
Hypocrites! You know how to interpret the appearance of the sky and the earth. Why, then, do you not know how to interpret this time?
And why do you not judge for yourselves what is right?

For as you go with the one bringing a case against you, while he is on the road, make an effort to settle with him, so that he does not drag you to a judge, and the judge hand you over to the officer, and the officer throw you into prison.
I tell you, you will not come out of there until you have paid your last small coin.
At that time, some people were telling him about the Galileans whose blood Pilate had mixed with their sacrifices.
He answered them, "Do you think that these Galileans sinned more than all the other Galileans because they suffered these things?"
I tell you, no. But unless you repent, you will all perish as they did.
Or those eighteen people on whom the tower in Siloam fell and whom it killed—do you think they were more guilty than all the people living in Jerusalem?
I tell you, no. But unless you repent, you will all perish as they did.
He told this parable: "Someone had a fig tree planted in his vineyard. He came looking for its fruit but found none on it."
He said to the gardener, “Look, for three years I have been coming to look for fruit on this fig tree, and I find none. So cut it down. Why should it also waste the soil?”
But he answered him, "Sir, leave it alone for this year too, until I dig around it and put manure on it."
If it bears fruit next year, leave it; if not, cut it down.
He was teaching in one of the synagogues on the Sabbath.
And there was a woman who had had a spirit of illness for eighteen years. She was bent over and could not straighten herself up at all.
When Jesus saw her, he called her over and said to her, “Woman, you are freed from your illness.”
He laid his hand on her, and immediately she stood upright and began giving glory to God.

But the synagogue leader, indignant because Jesus had healed on the Sabbath, responded by saying to the crowd, “There are six days on which work should be done. Come on those days and be healed, and do not come on the Sabbath day.”
But the Lord answered him, "Hypocrites! Does not each of you untie his ox or his donkey from its feeding trough on the Sabbath and lead it away to give it water?"
But this woman is a daughter of Abraham, whom Satan has bound for eighteen years. Should she not be freed from this bond on the Sabbath day?
As he said these things, all his opponents were put to shame, and the whole crowd rejoiced at all the glorious things he was doing.
Then he said, “What is the kingdom of God like, and what shall I compare it to?”
It is like a mustard seed that a man took and planted in his garden. It grew and became a tree, and the birds of the sky settled under its branches.
Again he said, “What shall I compare the kingdom of God to?”
“It is like yeast that a woman took and put into three measures of flour until the whole batch was leavened.”
He traveled through towns and villages, teaching as he went up to Jerusalem.
They said to him, “Lord, are only a few people going to be saved?” He said to them:
“Strive to enter through the narrow gate. I tell you, many will seek to enter and will not be able to.

“Once the master decides to get up and shut the door, you will begin knocking at the door while standing outside, saying, ‘Lord, open it for us!’ But he will answer you, ‘I do not know you or where you come from.’
“Then you will begin saying, ‘We ate and drank in your presence, and you taught us in our streets.’
“And he will say to you, ‘I do not know you or where you come from. Go away from me, all you who practice injustice!’
“There will be weeping and grinding of teeth there when you see Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, and all the prophets in the kingdom of God, while you yourselves are thrown out.
“People will come from the east and the west, from the north and the south, and recline at the table in the kingdom of God.
“Look, the last will be first, and the first will be last.”
At that very hour, some Pharisees approached him and said, “Go away and leave this place, because Herod wants to kill you.”
He answered them, “Go and tell that fox, ‘Look, I am casting out demons and performing healings today and tomorrow, and the day after tomorrow I will finish.’
“Nevertheless, I must spend today and tomorrow here and go the day after tomorrow, because it is not possible for a prophet to die outside Jerusalem.
“Jerusalem, Jerusalem, you who kill the prophets and stone those sent to you! How often I wanted to gather your children together, as a bird gathers its young under its wings, but you were unwilling!
“Look, your house will be left to you. I tell you, you will not see me until you say, ‘Blessed is the one who comes in the name of the Lord!’”
Now when he went into the house of a leader of the Pharisees on the Sabbath to eat a meal, they were watching him closely.
There was a man in front of him who suffered from swelling caused by fluid retention.
Jesus spoke to the experts in the law and the Pharisees, saying, “Is it lawful to heal on the Sabbath, or is it not lawful?”
But they remained silent. He took hold of the man, healed him, and sent him away.
He said to them, “Which of you, if his son or his ox falls into a well, will not immediately pull him out on the Sabbath day?”
And they were unable to answer him about these things.
He told a parable to the invited guests when he saw how they chose the places of honor for themselves. He said to them:
“When someone invites you, do not recline in the place of honor, in case he has invited someone more honored than you.
“Then the person who invited both you and him will come and tell you, ‘Give this man your place.’ Then, in shame, you will begin to take the lowest place.

“Instead, when you are invited, go and recline in the lowest place, so that when the person who invited you comes, he will say to you, ‘Friend, move up higher.’ Then you will be honored in the presence of all those reclining at the table with you.”
For everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, and whoever humbles himself will be exalted.

He also said to the man who had invited him, “When you give a lunch or dinner, do not invite your friends, your brothers, your relatives, or your rich neighbors, lest they invite you in return and you receive repayment.
Instead, when you give a feast, invite the poor, those with disabilities, the lame, and the blind.
Then you will be blessed, because they have nothing with which to repay you. For you will be repaid at the resurrection of the righteous.”
One of those reclining at the table with him heard this and said to him, “Blessed is the person who will eat bread in the kingdom of God!”
But he said to him, “A man gave a great dinner and invited many people.
At the time of the dinner, he sent his servant to tell those who had been invited, ‘Come, because everything is ready.’
But they all began making excuses at once. The first said to him, ‘I have bought a field, and I must go out to see it. Please excuse me.’
Another said to him, ‘I have bought five pairs of oxen, and I am going to test them. Please excuse me.’
Another said, ‘I have married a woman, and for this reason I cannot come.’

The servant came and reported these things to his master. Then the master became angry and said to his servant, ‘Go out quickly into the streets and lanes of the city, and bring the poor, those with disabilities, the blind, and the lame in here.’
The servant said, ‘Master, what you commanded has been done, and there is still room.’
The master said to the servant, ‘Go out to the roads and paths, and compel people to come in, so that my house will be filled.
I tell you that none of those who were invited will taste my dinner.’”
Large crowds were traveling with him. He turned and said to them,
“Whoever comes to me and does not hate his father and mother, his wife and children, his brothers and sisters, and even his own life, cannot be my disciple.
And whoever does not carry his cross daily and follow me cannot be my disciple.
For which of you, wanting to build a tower, will not first sit down and calculate the cost to see whether he has enough to finish it?
Otherwise, he might lay a foundation and be unable to finish it, and everyone who sees it will laugh at him,
saying, ‘This man began to build and could not finish.’
Or what king, going to fight another king, will not first sit down and consider whether he can confront with ten thousand men the one coming against him with twenty thousand?
If he cannot, he will send messengers while the other king is still far away, pleading, ‘Make peace.’
In the same way, anyone among you who does not give up all his possessions cannot be my disciple.
Salt is good, but if even the salt becomes tasteless, what will restore its saltiness?
It is useful neither for the soil nor for the manure heap; people throw it out. Whoever has ears to hear should listen.”
All the tax collectors and sinners were coming near him to listen to him.
The Pharisees and the teachers of the law were all grumbling, saying, “This man welcomes sinners and eats with them.”
Then he told this parable, saying:
“Which of you, if he has a hundred sheep and loses one of them, will not leave the ninety-nine in the wilderness and go looking for the one until he finds it?
And when he finds it, he puts it on his shoulders, rejoicing.
When he comes home, he calls his friends and neighbors together and says to them, ‘Rejoice with me, because I have found my sheep that was lost.’
I tell you, in the same way there is more joy over one sinner who repents than over ninety-nine righteous people who do not need repentance.
