“Or what woman who has ten drachmas and loses one of them will not light the lamp, sweep the house, and search carefully until she finds it?
And when she finds it, she calls her friends and neighbors together, saying, ‘Rejoice with me, because I have found the drachma that I lost.’
I tell you, in the same way there is joy in the presence of God’s angels over one sinner who repents.”
Then he said, “A man had two sons.
The younger of them said to his father, ‘Father, give me the share of the property that belongs to me.’ So he divided his possessions between them.
Not many days later, the younger son gathered everything he had and went away to a distant country. There he squandered his property by living extravagantly.
When he had spent everything, a severe famine struck that country, and he began to be in need.
He went and attached himself to a citizen of that country, who sent him to his field to tend pigs.
He longed to satisfy his hunger with the carob pods that the pigs ate, but no one gave him anything.
Then he thought things over and said, ‘How many of my father’s hired workers have plenty of bread, while I am dying of hunger here!
I will get up and go to my father and say to him, “Father, I have sinned against heaven and before you.
I am no longer worthy to be called your son. Treat me like one of these hired workers.”’
So he got up and came to his father. While he was still far away, his father saw him and felt compassion for him. He ran, threw his arms around his neck, and kissed him.
His son said to him, “Father, I have sinned against heaven and before you. I am no longer worthy to be called your son.”
Then the father said to his servants, ‘Quickly, bring out the fine robe and put it on him. Put a ring on his hand and sandals on his feet.
Bring the fattened calf and slaughter it, and eat and celebrate.
For this son of mine was dead and has come to life; he was lost, and I have found him.’ And they began to celebrate.
His older son was in the field. As he came back and approached the house, he heard music and dancing.
He called one of the servants and asked him, ‘What is all this?’
He said to him, “Your brother has come, and your father has slaughtered the fattened calf for him because he received him back safe and sound.”
But he became angry and refused to go inside. His father came out and pleaded with him.

He answered his father, “Look, I have served you for so many years and have never disobeyed any of your commands. Yet you have never given me even a young goat so that I could celebrate with my friends.
But when this son of yours came, who consumed your possessions with prostitutes, you slaughtered the fattened calf for him.”
He said to him, “My son, you are always with me, and everything of mine is yours.”
But we ought to rejoice and celebrate, because this brother of yours was dead and has come to life. He was lost, and I have found him.
He also said to his disciples, “There was a rich man who had a manager, and the manager was accused of squandering his possessions.
He called him and said to him, ‘What is this I hear about you? Give me an account of your management, for you can no longer be manager.’
The manager said to himself, ‘What will I do, since my master is taking the management away from me? I am not strong enough to dig, and I am ashamed to beg.
I know what I will do so that, when I am removed from the management, people will welcome me into their homes.’
He called his master’s debtors one by one and said to the first, ‘How much do you owe my master?’
He said, ‘A hundred baths of oil.’ He said to him, ‘Take your bill, sit down quickly, and write fifty.’
Then he said to another, ‘And you, how much do you owe?’ He said, ‘A hundred kors of wheat.’ He said, ‘Take your bill and write eighty.’
The master praised the dishonest manager because he had acted shrewdly. For the children of this age are wiser in dealing with their own generation than the children of light.
I too tell you: make friends for yourselves through unrighteous wealth, so that when it runs out, they will welcome you into eternal dwellings.
Whoever is faithful with a little is also faithful with much, and whoever is dishonest with a little is also dishonest with much.
So if you have not been faithful with unrighteous wealth, who will entrust you with what is real?
And if you have not been faithful with what belongs to someone else, who will give you what belongs to you?
No one can serve two masters. For either he will hate one and love the other, or he will hold on to one and despise the other. You cannot serve God and wealth.”
The Pharisees, who loved money, heard all these things and mocked him.
He said to them, “You are the ones who justify yourselves before people, but God knows your hearts. For pride among people is detestable in God’s sight.
The Law and the Prophets lasted until John. Since that time, the good news of the kingdom of God has been proclaimed, and everyone forces their way into it.
But it is easier for heaven and earth to pass away than for a single stroke of the Law to fall away.
Everyone who divorces his wife and marries another woman commits adultery, and anyone who marries a woman whose husband has divorced her commits adultery.
There was a rich man whose name was Nineveh. He used to dress in purple and fine linen and celebrate lavishly every day.
There was a poor man named Lazarus, who lay at his gate, covered with sores.
He longed to fill himself with what fell from the rich man’s table. Even the dogs would come and lick his sores.
The poor man died and was carried away by the angels into Abraham’s embrace. The rich man also died and was buried.
In the underworld, while he was in torment, he looked up and saw Abraham far away, with Lazarus in his arms.
He called out, saying, “Father Abraham, have mercy on me. Send Lazarus to dip the tip of his finger in water and cool my tongue, because I am suffering in this fire.”
But Abraham said, “My son, remember that you received your good things during your life, while Lazarus received bad things. Now he is comforted here, while you are tormented.”
“Besides all this, a great chasm has been fixed between us and you, so that those who want to cross from here to you cannot, nor can anyone cross from your side to us.”
He said, “Then I beg you, my father, to send him to my father’s house,”
“because I have five brothers, so that he can warn them, and they too will not come to this place of torment.”
But Abraham said to him, “They have Moses and the prophets. Let them listen to them.”
He said, “No, Father Abraham, but if someone goes to them from the dead, they will repent.”
But he said to him, “If they will not listen to Moses and the prophets, then even if someone rises from the dead, they will not listen to him.”
He said to his disciples, “It is difficult for things that cause people to sin not to come, but woe to the person through whom they come!”
“It would be better for him to have a millstone tied around his neck and be thrown into the sea than to cause one of these little ones to sin.”
“Watch yourselves. If your brother sins, rebuke him, and if he repents, forgive him.”
“Even if he sins against you seven times in a day and returns to you seven times in the day, saying, ‘I repent,’ you must forgive him.”
The apostles said to the Lord, “Increase our faith.”
The Lord said to them, “If you had faith the size of a mustard seed, you would say to this mulberry tree, ‘Be uprooted and planted in the sea,’ and it would obey you.”
“Which of you, having a slave plowing or tending the flock, would say to him immediately when he comes in from the field, ‘Come and recline to eat’?”
“Would he not instead say to him, ‘Prepare something for me to eat, tie up your clothing, and serve me until I have eaten and drunk? After that, you may eat and drink.’”
“Is the slave thanked because he did what he was commanded to do?”
“It is the same with you: when you have done everything you were commanded to do, say, ‘We are useless slaves. We have done what we were obliged to do.’”
As he was traveling to Jerusalem, he was passing through Samaria and Galilee.
As he was entering a village, ten men with leprosy met him. They stood at a distance,
calling out, “Jesus, Master, have mercy on us!”
When he saw them, he said to them, “Go and show yourselves to the priests.” As they went, they were cleansed.
When one of them saw that he had been cleansed, he turned back, glorifying God in a loud voice.
He fell facedown at his feet, thanking him. He was a Samaritan.
Jesus answered, “Were not the ten cleansed? Where are the other nine?”
“Was no one found who returned to give glory to God except this foreigner?”
He said to him, “Get up and go.”
When the Pharisees asked him when the kingdom of God was coming, he answered them, “The kingdom of God does not come through observation.”
“Nor will they say, ‘Look, here it is!’ or ‘There it is!’ For look, the kingdom of God is within you.”
He said to his disciples, “Days are coming when you will long to see one of the days of the Son of Man, but you will not see it.”
“They will say to you, ‘Look, he is here!’ or ‘In this place!’ Do not run out.”
“For just as lightning shines beneath the sky and lights up the earth, so it will be with the Son of Man.”
“But first he must suffer many things and be rejected by this generation.”
And just as it happened in the days of Noah, so it will happen in the days of the Son of Man.

“For just as it happened in the days of Noah, at the end of the flood, they were eating, drinking, taking wives, and living with husbands until the day Noah entered the ark. The flood came and destroyed them all.”
“And again, just as it happened in the days of Lot: they were eating, drinking, buying, selling, planting, and building.”
“But on the day Lot left Sodom, fire and sulfur rained down from heaven and destroyed everyone.”
“That is how it will be on the day when the Son of Man is revealed.”
“In those days, anyone who is on the rooftop, with his belongings in his house, must not come down to take them. And anyone who is in the field must not turn back.”
“Remember Lot’s wife.”
“Whoever seeks to preserve his life will lose it, and whoever loses it will keep it alive.”
“I tell you, on that night two people will be in one bed. One will be taken and the other left.”
Two women will be grinding together; one will be taken and the other left.
They answered him, “Where, Lord?” He said to them, “Wherever the body is, the eagles will gather around it.”
He told them a parable about the need to pray at all times and not lose heart.
He said, “There was a judge in a city who neither feared God nor respected people.”
There was a widow in that city who kept coming to him and saying, “Give me justice against my opponent.”
“For a long time he was unwilling. But afterward he said to himself, ‘Even though I do not fear God or respect people,’
‘yet because this widow keeps troubling me, I will grant her justice, so that she will not keep coming forever and wearing me out.’
The Lord said, “Listen to what the unjust judge said.”
“Then will God not grant justice to his chosen ones who cry out to him day and night, and be patient with them?”
“I tell you that he will grant them justice quickly. But when the Son of Man comes, will he find faith on the earth?”
He told this parable to some people who trusted in themselves that they were righteous and looked down on everyone else:
“Two men went up to the temple to pray. One was a Pharisee, and the other was a tax collector.
The Pharisee stood and prayed these words: ‘God, I thank you that I am not like other people—robbers, people who take things by force, adulterers—or like this tax collector.
I fast twice a week, and I give a tenth of everything I acquire.
But the tax collector stood far away and would not even lift his eyes to heaven. Instead, he beat his chest, saying, ‘God, forgive me, a sinner.’
I tell you, this man went down to his house declared righteous rather than the other. For everyone who exalts himself will be humbled, but whoever humbles himself will be exalted.
People were bringing little children to him so that he would touch them. When his disciples saw them, they rebuked them.
But Jesus called them to him, saying, “Let the little children come to me, and do not stop them, for the kingdom of God belongs to those who are like them.
Truly I tell you, whoever does not receive the kingdom of God like a little child will never enter it.”
A ruler asked him, “Good teacher, what must I do to inherit eternal life?”
Jesus said to him, “Why do you call me good? No one is good except one—God.
You know the commandments: Do not commit adultery. Do not murder. Do not steal. Do not give false testimony. Honor your father and your mother.”
He said to him, “I have kept all these since my youth.”
Jesus answered him, “You still lack one thing. Sell everything you have and give it to the poor, and you will have treasure in heaven. Then come and follow me.”
When he heard this, he became sad, for he was very rich.
Jesus looked at him and said, “See how hard it is for those who have wealth to enter the kingdom of God!
For it is easier for a camel to pass through the eye of a sewing needle than for a rich person to enter the kingdom of God.”
Those who heard this said, “Who, then, can be saved?”
He said to them, “What is impossible for people is possible for God.”
Peter said, “Look, we have left behind what belongs to us and followed you.”
He said to them, “Truly I tell you, there is no one who has left behind a house, a wife, a brother, parents, or children for the sake of the kingdom of God
Will he not receive them sevenfold in this time, and eternal life in the age to come?
He took the twelve and said to them, “Look, I am going up to Jerusalem, and everything written by the prophets will be fulfilled for the Son of Man.
For he will be handed over to the Gentiles to be mocked, and they will insult him and spit in his face.
They will whip him and kill him, and he will rise on the third day.”
But they understood none of these things. This saying was hidden from them, and they did not understand what he was saying.
As he approached Jericho, a blind man was sitting beside the road, begging.
He heard the crowd and asked what was happening.
They told him that Jesus of Nazareth was passing by.
He cried out, saying, “Jesus, Son of David, have mercy on me!”
Those walking ahead rebuked him and told him to be quiet. But he cried out even louder, saying, “Son of David, have mercy on me!”
Jesus stopped and ordered them to bring him to him. When he came near, Jesus asked him,
“What do you want me to do for you?” He said, “Lord, let me see again.”
Jesus said to him, “See again! Your faith has saved you.”
Immediately he could see again, and he followed him, giving glory to God. When all the people saw this, they praised God.
He entered Jericho and passed through it.
There was a man named Zacchaeus. He was a chief tax collector and was rich.
He was trying to find out who Jesus was, but he could not because of the crowd, since he was short.
He ran ahead and climbed a sycamore tree to see him, because he was going to pass that way.
When Jesus came to the place, he looked up and said to him, “Zacchaeus, hurry and come down, for I must stay at your house today.”
He hurried down and welcomed him joyfully.
When they all saw this, they grumbled, saying, “He has gone in to stay with a sinful man.”
Zacchaeus stood and said to the Lord, “Look, Lord, I give half of my possessions to the poor, and whatever I have extorted from anyone, I will repay four times over.”
Jesus said to him, “Today salvation has come to this house, because he too is a son of Abraham.
For the Son of Man came to seek and save what was lost.”
As they listened to these things, he went on to tell a parable, because they were near Jerusalem and thought that the kingdom of God would appear immediately.
So he said, “A man of noble birth went to a distant country to receive a kingdom for himself and then return.
He called ten of his servants and gave them ten minas. He said to them, ‘Do business until I come back.’
But his fellow townspeople hated him and sent a delegation after him, saying, ‘We do not want this man to reign over us.’
When he returned after receiving the kingdom, he ordered that the servants to whom he had given the money be called to him, so that he could find out what business they had done.
The first came and said, ‘Master, your mina has earned ten minas.’
He said to him, ‘Well done, good servant! Because you have been faithful in a small matter, you shall have authority over ten cities.’
The second came and said, ‘Master, your mina has made five minas.’
He said to this one too, ‘You too shall be over five cities.’
Then the other man came and said, “Master, here is your mina, which I kept wrapped in a handkerchief.
For I was afraid of you, because you are a stern man. You take what you did not put down and reap what you did not sow.”
He said to him, “I will judge you by your own words, you wicked servant. If you knew that I am a stern man, taking what I did not put down and reaping what I did not sow,
why did you not put my money in the bank, so that I could come and collect it with its interest?”
Then he said to those standing there, “Take the mina from him and give it to the man who has the ten minas.”
They said to him, “Master, he has ten minas!”
But he said to them, “I tell you that everyone who has will be given more, but from the one who has nothing, even what he has will be taken away.
But bring here those enemies of mine who did not want me to reign over them, and slaughter them in front of me.”
After saying these things, he walked ahead of them, going up to Jerusalem.
When he approached Bethphage and Bethany, at the mountain called the Mount of Olives, he sent two of his disciples,
saying, “Go into the village in front of you. When you enter it, you will find a colt tied up, which no one has ever ridden. Untie it and bring it.
If anyone asks you, ‘Why are you untying it?’ say, ‘Its master needs it.’”
Those who had been sent went and found things just as he had told them.
As they were untying the colt, its owners said to them, “Why are you untying the colt?”
They said, “Its master needs it.”
They brought it to Jesus, spread their clothes over the colt, and helped Jesus onto it.
As they went along, they spread their clothes on the road.
As he drew near, coming down the Mount of Olives, the whole crowd of his disciples began joyfully praising God in a loud voice for all the miracles they had seen,
saying, “Blessed is the king who comes in the name of the Lord! Peace in heaven and glory in the highest!”
Some of the Pharisees in the crowd said to him, “Teacher, rebuke your disciples.”
He answered, “I tell you, if these people keep quiet, the stones will cry out.”
As he drew near and saw the city, he wept over it.
saying, “If only you too had understood on this day the things that bring you peace! But now they are hidden from your eyes.
For days are coming upon you when your enemies will build a siege ramp around you and hem you in on every side.
They will strike you and your children within you down to the ground. They will not leave one stone on another within you, because you did not recognize the time when you were visited.”
When he entered the temple, he began driving out those who were selling.
He said to them, “It is written, ‘My house will be a house of prayer,’ but you are making it a den of robbers.”
He was teaching every day in the temple. But the chief priests and the scribes, together with the leaders of the people, were looking for a way to kill him.
They could not find what to do to him, because all the people delighted in listening to him.
One day, while he was teaching the people in the temple and proclaiming the good news, the chief priests came up to him with the scribes and the elders.
They said to him, “Tell us, by what authority are you doing these things? Or who gave you this authority?”
He answered them, “I too will ask you a question, if you will answer it for me.
Where did John’s baptism come from? Was it from heaven or from human beings?”
They discussed it among themselves, saying, “If we say, ‘From heaven,’ he will say to us, ‘Then why did you not believe him?’
But if we say, ‘From human beings,’ all the people will stone us, because they are convinced that John was a prophet.”
They answered, “We do not know where it comes from.”
Jesus said to them, “Neither will I tell you by what authority I am doing these things.”
He began to tell the people this parable: “A man planted a vineyard, leased it to farmers, and went away for a long time.
At harvest time he sent a servant to the farmers so that they would give him some of the vineyard’s produce. But the farmers beat him and sent him away empty-handed.
He then sent another servant. But they beat this one too, humiliated him, and sent him away empty-handed.
He then sent a third. But they wounded this one too and threw him out.
The owner of the vineyard said, ‘What shall I do? I will send my beloved son. Perhaps they will respect this one.’
When the farmers saw him, they discussed it with one another, saying, “This is the heir. Let us kill him so that the inheritance will become ours.”
But they threw him out of the vineyard and killed him. What, then, will the owner of the vineyard do to them?
He will come and destroy the farmers and give the vineyard to others.” When they heard this, they said, “May that never happen!”
He looked directly at them and said to them, “What, then, does this passage mean: ‘The stone that the builders rejected has become the cornerstone’?
Everyone who falls on that stone will be shattered, and anyone it falls on will be crushed.”
The chief priests and the scribes tried to lay their hands on him and arrest him that very hour, but they were afraid of the people, because they realized that he had told this parable against them.
They watched him and sent spies who pretended to be righteous, so that they could catch him in something he said and hand him over to the governor’s rule and authority.
They asked him, “Teacher, we know that you speak and teach correctly and show no partiality, but teach the way of God truthfully.
Is it lawful for us to pay taxes to the emperor, or is it not lawful?”
But he recognized their cunning and said to them:
“Show me a stater coin.” They brought it out. He said, “Whose image and inscription are on it?” They said to him, “The emperor’s.”
He said to them, “Then give the emperor what belongs to the emperor, and God what belongs to God.”
They could not catch him in anything he said in front of the people. They were amazed at his answer and fell silent.
Some of the Sadducees, who say there will be no resurrection, came forward and said,
“Teacher, Moses wrote for us that if a man's brother dies, leaving a wife but no children, his brother should marry his wife and raise up offspring for his brother.
Now there were seven brothers. The first married a woman and died without children.
And the second
and the third married her. Likewise, all seven died without leaving children.
After all of them, the woman also died.
In the resurrection, whose wife will she be? For all seven married her.”
Jesus said to them, “The people of this age marry wives and live with husbands.
But those considered worthy to obtain that age and the resurrection from the dead neither marry wives nor live with husbands.
For they can no longer die, because they are equal to angels. They are children of God and children of the resurrection.
Moses also spoke of the dead rising, in the passage about the bush, where the Lord is called ‘the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob.’
He is not the God of the dead but of the living, for all are alive to him.”
Some of the scribes answered him, “Teacher, you have spoken well.”
For after that they did not dare to ask him anything.
He said to them, “How can you say that the Christ is David's son?
For David himself says in the book of Psalms, ‘The Lord said to my Lord, “Sit at my right hand.”’
Until I make your enemies a footstool for your feet.
David therefore calls him ‘my Lord.’ How is he his son?”
While all the people were listening, he said to his disciples,
“Beware of the scribes, who like to walk around in robes and love greetings in the marketplaces, the foremost seats in the synagogues, and the places of honor at banquets.
They devour widows' houses and pray with great pretense. They will receive a harsher judgment.”
He looked up and saw the rich putting their gifts into the treasury.
He also saw a poor widow putting two small coins there.
He said, “Truly I tell you, this poor widow has put in more than all of them.
For all of them gave their gifts out of their surplus, but she, out of her poverty, put in everything she had.”
Some were speaking about the temple, saying that it was adorned with beautiful stones and dedicated gifts.
He said, “As for all these things you see, days are coming when no stone here will be left on another stone without being torn down.”
They asked him, “Teacher, when will these things happen, and what will be the sign that these things are going to happen?”
But he said, “Be careful not to be misled. For many will come in my name, saying, ‘I am he,’ and, ‘The time has drawn near.’ Do not follow them.
When you hear of wars and upheavals, do not be afraid. These things must happen first, but the end will not come immediately.”
Then he said to them, “Nation will rise against nation, and kingdom against kingdom.
There will be great earthquakes and famines in various places, and there will be plagues. There will be terrifying things and great signs from heaven.
But before all these things, they will seize you and persecute you, handing you over to synagogues and prisons and bringing you before kings and governors because of my name.
This will be an opportunity for you to testify.
So resolve in your hearts not to rehearse your defense.
For I will give you words and wisdom that none of your opponents will be able to resist or answer.
You will be handed over by your parents, your brothers, your relatives, and your friends, and they will kill some of you.
Everyone will hate you because of my name.
And not a hair will fall from your head.
But through your endurance you will gain your lives.
When you see Jerusalem surrounded by soldiers, then know that its devastation has drawn near.
Then those in Judea must flee to the mountains, those inside the city must leave it, and those in the countryside must not enter it.
For these are the days of vengeance, when everything written will be fulfilled.
But woe to those who are pregnant and those who are nursing in those days! For there will be great distress on the earth and great anger from Pilate.
They will fall by the edge of the sword and be taken captive to all the nations. The nations will walk through Jerusalem until the times of the nations are fulfilled.
There will be signs in the sun, the moon, and the stars, and the nations gathered on earth will be bewildered by the noise and movement of the sea.
People will lose heart from fear and from anticipating what is coming upon the inhabited world, for the powers and the heavens will be shaken.
Then they will see the Son of Man coming in a cloud with power and great glory.
When these things begin to happen, look up and lift your heads, because your deliverance has drawn near.”
Then he told them a parable: “Look at the fig tree and all the trees.
When they begin to sprout, you see them for yourselves and know that summer has drawn near.
In the same way, when you see these things happening, know that the kingdom of God has drawn near.
Truly I tell you, this generation will not pass away before all these things happen.
Heaven and earth will pass away, but my words will not pass away.
Watch yourselves, so that your hearts do not become weighed down with overeating, drunkenness, and the worries of life, and that day does not come upon you suddenly,
like a trap. For it will come upon everyone who lives on the face of the whole earth.
But stay awake at all times, praying that you may have the strength to escape all these things that will happen and to stand before the Son of Man.
During the day he would teach in the temple, but at night he would go out and stay on the mountain called the Mount of Olives.
And all the people would come to him early in the morning in the temple to listen to him.
Now the Festival of Unleavened Bread, which is called Passover, drew near.
And the chief priests and the scribes were looking for a way to destroy him, for they were afraid of the people.
Then Satan entered Judas, who was called Iscariot and was counted among the twelve.
He went and spoke with the chief priests and the officers about how to hand him over to them.
And they were glad and agreed with him to give him money.
He agreed and looked for an opportunity to hand him over to them without a crowd present.
Then the day of Unleavened Bread drew near, on which the Passover sacrifice had to be slaughtered.
He sent Peter and John, saying to them, “Go and prepare the Passover for us so that we may eat it.”
They said to him, “Where do you want us to prepare it for you?”
He said to them, “Look, when you enter this city, a man carrying a jar of water will meet you. Follow him into the house he enters.”
“And say to the owner of the house, ‘The teacher says to you: Where is my guest room, where I will eat the Passover with my disciples?’
And he will show you a large furnished upstairs room. Prepare it for me there.”
They went and found it just as he had told them, and they prepared the Passover.
When the hour came, he reclined at the table with the twelve.
He said to them, “I have eagerly desired to eat this Passover [?] with you before I die.
For I tell you, I will not eat it until it is fulfilled in the kingdom of God.”
He took a cup, blessed it, and said to them, “Take this and share it among yourselves.
For I tell you, from now on I will not drink from this fruit of the grapevine until the kingdom of God comes.”
And he took bread, blessed it, broke it, and gave it to them, saying, “This is my body, which will be given for you. Do this in remembrance of me.”
And likewise the cup after they had eaten, saying, “This cup is the new covenant in my blood, which will be poured out for you.”
But look, the hand of the one who will betray me is with me on the table.
For the Son of Man will go as it is written for him, but woe to that man through whom he will be handed over!
They began discussing with one another which of them would do this.
A dispute arose among them about which of them was the greatest.
He said to them, “The kings of the nations rule over them, and those who exercise authority over them are called benefactors.”
But you must not be like this. Instead, let the greatest among you become like the youngest, and the one who leads you like the one who serves.
For who is greater: the one reclining at the table or the one serving? Is it not the one reclining at the table? But I am among you as one who serves.
You are the ones who have stayed with me through my trials.
I, in turn, appoint a kingdom for you, just as my Father appointed one for me,
so that you may eat and drink at my table in my kingdom, and sit on thrones judging the twelve tribes of Israel.
Simon, Simon, look, Satan has asked to sift all of you like wheat.
But I have prayed for you so that your faith will not fail. You, in turn, return and strengthen your brothers.
But he said to him, “Lord, I am ready to go with you to prison and to death.”
But he said to him, “I tell you, Peter, a rooster will not crow today until you have denied me three times, saying, ‘I do not know him.’”
And he said to them, “When I sent you out without a money bag, a traveling bag, or sandals, did you lack anything?” They said, “No.”
He said to them, “But now, whoever has a money bag should take it, and likewise whoever has a traveling bag. Anyone who has none should sell his garment and buy himself a sword.”
For I tell you that this passage written about me must be fulfilled in me: ‘I was counted among the lawless.’ For what is appointed for me has been fulfilled.
They said, “Lord, look, there are two swords here.” He said to them, “They are enough.”
He went out and went to the Mount of Olives, as was his custom, and his disciples followed him.
When he arrived at the place, he said to them, “Pray that you do not enter into temptation.”
He withdrew from them about a stone’s throw and bent his knees.
He said, “My Father, if you are willing, let this cup pass from me. Nevertheless, let your will be done, not mine.”
He rose from prayer and came to the disciples. He found them sleeping because of their grief.
He said to them, “Why are you sleeping? Get up and pray so that you do not enter into temptation.”
While he was still speaking, a crowd arrived. The man called Judas, who was one of the twelve, was walking ahead of them. He approached Jesus to kiss him.
Jesus said to him, “Judas, will you betray the Son of Man with a kiss?”
When those around him saw what was about to happen, they said to him, “Lord, shall we strike with the sword?”
And one of them struck the high priest’s slave and cut off his right ear.
But Jesus answered and said to him, “Stop now.” He touched his ear and healed him.
Jesus said to the chief priests, the temple officers, and the elders who had come against him, “Have you come out after me as though after a robber, with your swords and clubs?”
Every day, while I was in the temple, you did not lay your hands on me. But this is your hour and your authority—the darkness.
They seized him, led him away, and brought him into the high priest’s house. Peter followed him at a distance.
When they had lit a fire for themselves in the middle of the courtyard and sat down, Peter sat among them.
When a servant girl saw him sitting beside the fire, she looked closely at his face and said, “This man was with him too.”
But he denied it, saying, “Woman, I do not know him.”
A little later, someone else saw him and said, “You too are one of them.” Peter said, “Man, no!”
When an hour had passed, someone else insisted, saying, “This man really was with him, for he is also a Galilean.”
Peter said, “Man, I do not know what you are talking about.” Immediately, while he was still speaking, the rooster crowed.
The Lord turned and looked at Peter. Peter remembered the Lord’s words, how he had said, “Before a rooster crows today, you will deny me three times.”
He went outside and wept bitterly.
The men who were holding him mocked him and beat him.
They covered his face and questioned him, saying, “Prophesy for us, Christ! Who hit you?”
They also said many other things against him, insulting him.
When morning came, the elders of the people, the chief priests, and the scribes gathered together, and they brought him before the council.
They said, “Are you the Christ? Tell us.” But he said to them, “If I tell you, you will not believe.
And if I question you, you will not answer me.
From now on, the Son of Man will be seated at the right hand of the power of God.”
They all said, “Are you the Son of God?” He said to them, “You yourselves say that I am.”
They said, “What do we need testimony for now? We ourselves have heard it from his mouth.”
Then the whole crowd rose and brought him before Pilate.
They began to accuse him, saying, “We found this man stirring up our nation and forbidding the payment of taxes to the king, saying, ‘I am the king, the Christ.’”
Pilate questioned him, saying, “Are you the king of the Jews?” He answered, “You say so.”
Pilate said to the crowd, “I find no guilt in this man.”
But they insisted, saying, “He stirs up the people by teaching throughout Judea, starting from Galilee and reaching here.”
When Pilate heard Galilee mentioned, he asked whether the man was a Galilean.
When he learned that he was under Herod’s jurisdiction, he sent him to Herod, who was also in Jerusalem during those days.
When Herod saw Jesus, he was very glad, for he had wanted to see him for a long time because he had heard about him, and he hoped to see him perform a sign.
He questioned him at length, but Jesus gave him no answer.
The chief priests and the scribes stood there, vehemently accusing him.
Herod and his soldiers treated him with contempt and mocked him. They dressed him in a white robe and sent him to Pilate.
Herod and Pilate became friends with each other that day, for previously they had been enemies.
Pilate called together the chief priests, the rulers, and the people.
He said to them, “You brought this man to me as someone who stirs up the people. Look, I have examined him before you and have found him guilty of none of the things you accuse him of.
Nor did Herod find anything against him, for he sent him to us. Look, he has done nothing deserving death.
So I will punish him and release him.”
But they all shouted, “Take this man away! Release Barabbas for us!”
He had been thrown into prison for an uprising that had taken place in the city and for murder.
Pilate spoke to them again, wanting to release Jesus.
But they shouted at him, “Crucify him! Crucify him!”
He said to them a third time, “Why, what evil has this man done? I have found no grounds for sentencing him to death. So I will punish him and release him.”
But they kept insisting with loud shouts, demanding, “Crucify him!” And their voices prevailed.
Pilate decided to grant their request.
He released the man who had been thrown into prison for the uprising and murder, the one they were asking for, but he handed Jesus over to their will.
As they led him out, they seized a man from Cyrene named Simon, who was coming in from the countryside. They put Jesus’ cross on him to carry it behind Jesus.
A large crowd of people followed him, along with women who were beating their breasts and mourning for him.
Jesus turned around and said to them, “Daughters of Jerusalem, do not weep for me. Instead, weep for yourselves and your children.
For look, days are coming when people will say, ‘Blessed are the barren women, the wombs that have not given birth, and the breasts that have not nursed.’
Then they will begin to say to the mountains, ‘Fall on us!’ and to the hills, ‘Cover us!’
For if they do these things to the green wood, what will happen to the dry wood?”
They also led out two other men, criminals, to be put to death with him.
When they came to the place called the Skull, they crucified him there, along with the two other criminals, one on his right and the other on his left.
They divided his clothes and cast lots for them.
The people stood watching, and the rulers also sneered at him, saying, “He saved others; let him save himself if he is the Christ, the chosen one, the Son of God.”
The soldiers also mocked him, approaching him with vinegar.
They said, “If you are the king of the Jews, save yourself!”
There was also an inscription above him: “This is the king of the Jews.”
One of the criminals hanging there insulted him, saying, “Aren’t you the Christ? Save yourself and us!”
But the other answered and rebuked him, saying, “Don’t you fear God, since we are under the same sentence?”
“We are being punished justly, for we are receiving what our deeds deserve. But this man has done nothing wrong.”
And he said, “Jesus, Lord, remember me when you come in your kingdom.”
He said to him, “Truly I tell you today that you will be with me in paradise.”
It was noon, and darkness came over the whole land until three in the afternoon.
As the sun was about to set, the curtain of the temple tore down the middle.
Jesus cried out in a loud voice and said, “My Father, I place my spirit in your hands.” After saying this, he breathed his last.
When the centurion saw what had happened, he praised God, saying, “This man really was righteous.”
And the crowds who had come to watch, when they saw what had happened, beat their chests and went back.
But all those who knew him stood at a distance, along with the women who had followed him from Galilee, watching these things.
Now there was a man named Joseph, a member of the council, a good and righteous man.
He had not agreed with their plan or their actions. He was from Arimathea, a Jewish town, and was waiting for the kingdom of God.
This man went to Pilate and asked for the body of Jesus.

He took him down, wrapped him in a linen cloth, and laid him in a tomb that had been cut out of rock, where no one had ever been laid. After he laid him there, they placed a stone against the entrance of the tomb, which even twenty men could barely roll.
It was the day of Preparation, with the Sabbath the next day.
The women who had come with him from Galilee followed behind and saw the tomb and how his body had been laid in it.
They went back and prepared spices and ointments. Then they rested on the Sabbath according to the commandment.

On the first day of the week, very early in the morning, they came to the tomb, bringing the spices they had prepared, with some others accompanying them. They were thinking to themselves, “Who will roll the stone away for us?”
But when they arrived, they found the stone rolled away from the tomb.
They went inside, but did not find the body of the Lord Jesus.
While they were bewildered about this, two men suddenly came up to them in shining clothes.
They became afraid and bowed their heads toward the ground. The men said to them, “Why are you looking for the living among the dead?”
“He is not here, but has risen. Remember how he spoke to you while he was still in Galilee,”
“saying, ‘The Son of Man must be handed over to sinful people and crucified, and rise on the third day.’”
And they remembered his words.
They returned from the tomb and told these things to the eleven and all the others.
They were Mary Magdalene, Joanna, Mary of James, and the other women with them. They were telling these things to the apostles.
These words seemed like nonsense to them, and they did not believe the women.
But Peter got up and went to the tomb. He looked inside and saw the cloths lying to one side. He went away, wondering to himself about what had happened.
And two of them were walking that same day to a village called Emmaus, sixty stadia away from Jerusalem.
They were talking with one another about all these things that had happened.
While they were talking and discussing these things, Jesus came near them and walked with them.
But their eyes were kept from recognizing him.
He said to them, “What are these things you are discussing with one another as you walk?” And they stood still, looking sad.
One of them, whose name was Cleopas, answered him, “Are you the only visitor to Jerusalem who does not know what has happened there in these days?”
He said to them, “What things?” They said to him, “The things about Jesus of Nazareth, who was a prophet, powerful in deed and word before God and all the people,
and how the chief priests and our rulers handed him over to be sentenced to death and crucified him.
But we were hoping that he was the one who would redeem Israel. Yet [?] all these things, today is the third day since these things happened.
Some women from among us also astonished us. They went to the tomb early in the morning,
but they did not find his body. They came back saying, ‘We saw a vision of angels,’ who were saying
that he had risen. And some of those with us went to the tomb and found it just as the women had said, but they did not see him.”
He said to them, “You foolish people, whose hearts are slow to believe everything the prophets said!
Wasn't it necessary for the Christ to suffer these things and enter into his glory?”
Then, beginning with Moses and all the prophets, he explained to them what concerned him in all the Scriptures.
And they entered the village they were going to, but he began walking farther away from them.
They held him back, saying, “Stay with us, because it is evening and the day is drawing to a close.” So he went in and stayed with them.
When he reclined at the table with them, he took a loaf of bread, blessed it, broke it, and gave it to them.
Their eyes were opened, and they recognized him, but he disappeared from their sight.
They said to one another, “Wasn't our heart veiled from us as he spoke with us on the road, explaining the Scriptures to us?”
They got up that very hour, grieving, and returned to Jerusalem. They found the eleven gathered together with those who were with them.
They were saying, “The Lord has truly risen and has appeared to Simon!”
They too told what had happened on the road and how he had revealed himself to them in the breaking of the bread.
While they were saying these things, he stood among them and said to them, “Peace be with you.”
But they were troubled and afraid, thinking they were seeing a spirit.
He said to them, “Why are you troubled, and why do doubts arise in your hearts?
Look at my hands and my feet: it is I myself. Touch me and see, because a spirit does not have bones and flesh, as you see that I have.”
And when he said this, [?] showed them his hands and his feet.
While they still did not believe because of their joy and were amazed, he said to them, “Do you have anything to eat here?”
They gave him a piece of roasted fish.
He took it and ate it in front of them.
He said to them, “These are my words that I spoke to you while I was still with you: everything written about me in the Law of Moses, the Prophets, and the Psalms must be fulfilled.”
Then he opened their minds so that they could know him and understand the Scriptures.
He said to them, “This is what is written: that Christ should do this and rise on the third day,
and that repentance should be proclaimed in his name for the forgiveness of sins to all nations, beginning with you in Jerusalem.
You are witnesses to these things.
I myself will send the Father's promise upon you. But stay in this city until you are clothed with power from heaven.”
He led them out as far as Bethany, raised his hands, and blessed them.
While he was blessing them, he parted from them and went up to heaven.
They worshiped him and returned to Jerusalem with great joy.
And they were continually in the temple, praising God.
